text: In `reduce(identity, operator)`, why does the identity value have to be genuinely neutral?
choices: Reducing an empty input returns it, so a wrong identity gives wrong answers only when the input is empty.
A non-neutral identity prevents the JIT from fusing the reduction with earlier stages.
The operator is applied to the identity twice when the stream is parallel.
The identity determines the result type, so a wrong one causes a class cast at run time.
explanation: 0 for addition, 1 for multiplication, `""` for concatenation. Choose wrong and every test with non-empty data passes, which is what makes it a durable bug. This is Chapter 13's accumulator passing with the accumulator as the only state — which is exactly why the pattern parallelizes, provided the operator is also associative.
